normal: Slower growth and smaller leaves are normal on a windowsill now: the light is weak. Some herbs, like parsley, keep cropping with enough light and warmth; short-lived ones fade.
tips: Light: your sunniest windowsill; don't leave it behind closed curtains at night.
Water: only when the top of the compost feels dry; a cool room needs it less often.
Warmth: off the radiator shelf and out of cold draughts; basil wants a warm room.
Picking: take a few leaves or shoot tips at a time, so it stays bushy.
because: the light is weakest now, and a herb indoors needs all it can get.
if_you_do: More light means sturdier growth instead of pale, stretched stems.

normal: Growth picks up as the days lengthen: new shoots and bigger leaves are normal now.
tips: Light: a bright windowsill; south or west facing suits most herbs.
Water: keep the compost moist but never soggy; it needs water more often as it grows.
Feeding: a balanced liquid feed now and then while it grows, not a high-potash one.
Pots: when it fills its pot, go only 5 to 10 cm wider.
because: it is growing again, and houseplant feeding starts in March.
if_you_do: Steadier growth and more leaves to pick through spring and summer.

normal: Fast growth is normal now, and some herbs try to flower or run to seed indoors.
tips: Light: bright, but hot midday sun through the glass can scorch soft leaves.
Water: check every day or two in hot weather; water in the morning if you can.
Picking: pinch out shoot tips often, so it stays bushy.
Feeding: carry on with a balanced feed until October.
because: hot sun through the glass can scorch soft leaves in summer.
if_you_do: Out of the midday glare, the leaves are less likely to scorch.

normal: Growth slows as the days shorten; that is normal on a windowsill. Short-lived herbs go pale in low light and may be near their end.
tips: Light: move it to your sunniest windowsill as the light drops.
Water: less often as growth slows; let the top of the compost dry first.
Warmth: once the heating comes on, keep it off the radiator shelf.
Feeding: from November, once a month at most.
because: the light is dropping fast, and a herb indoors needs all it can get.
if_you_do: More light means sturdier growth instead of pale, stretched stems.

normal: Little or no new growth is normal now. These herbs do better in a cool, bright room than a warm, dim one.
tips: Light: the brightest windowsill you have, ideally in a cool room.
Water: sparingly; let the top of the compost dry, and never let the pot stand in water.
Warmth: well away from radiators; a warm, dim room gives weak growth.
because: the light is weakest now, and these herbs want all of it.
if_you_do: More light means sturdier growth instead of pale, stretched stems.

normal: New shoots are normal now as the days lengthen.
tips: Light: as much as possible; a sunny windowsill.
Water: when the top of the compost is dry; it never wants to be soggy.
Pots: when it fills its pot, go only 5 to 10 cm wider.

normal: Steady growth is normal; these herbs like sun and compost that is never wet for long.
tips: Light: full sun suits them, but watch for scorch through the glass on the hottest days.
Water: when the top of the compost is dry; more often in hot spells.
Feeding: a balanced feed now and then, not a high-potash one.

normal: Growth slows as the days shorten; that is normal.
tips: Light: the sunniest spot you have as the light fades.
Water: less as growth slows; never let it sit wet.
Warmth: off the radiator shelf once the heating comes on.

normal: Little new growth is normal in winter: the light is low. Brown leaf edges can mean too little water or a radiator too close.
tips: Light: out of dark corners to a brighter spot, and not behind closed curtains at night.
Water: less than in summer, when the top of the compost is dry; use water at room temperature.
Air: central heating dries the air; stand it on a tray of damp gravel or group plants together.
Warmth: away from radiators, fires and cold draughts.
Feeding: little or none until March.
because: central heating dries the air, which some houseplants struggle with.
if_you_do: A tray of damp gravel or plants grouped together keep the air round the leaves moister.

normal: New leaves are normal now as the light improves.
tips: Light: bright, out of hot midday sun.
Water: more often as it grows; still let the top of the compost dry first.
Feeding: start again in March, following the label.
Repotting: spring is the time; most need a bigger pot every two to three years.
because: spring is the time to pot on, if the roots fill the pot or the compost dries out very fast.
if_you_do: A slightly bigger pot and fresh compost give it room to grow through summer.

normal: Steady new growth is normal now.
tips: Light: out of strong sun through the glass, which can scorch leaves.
Water: check more often in warm spells; never leave the pot standing in water.
Air: mist it often in hot weather, or use a tray of damp gravel.
Feeding: regularly until October, following the label.
because: it is growing, and houseplants are fed from March to October.

normal: Growth slows as the days shorten; that is normal.
tips: Light: move it closer to a window as the light drops.
Water: less often as growth slows.
Warmth: when the heating comes on, keep it off radiators and out of draughts.
Feeding: from November, once a month at most.
because: the light is dropping, and a brighter spot keeps it growing steadily.
if_you_do: More light in winter means less weak, stretched growth.

normal: A rest is normal now: no new growth, and compost dry for weeks, is fine until early March.
tips: Light: a sunny windowsill all year.
Water: little or none until March.
Warmth: fine in a heated room, but not on the radiator shelf; dry air doesn't bother it.

normal: Growth starts again from March as the light improves.
tips: Light: a sunny windowsill.
Water: when the compost is dry to the touch.
Repotting: spring is the time, into a pot only a little bigger.
because: spring is the time to repot, if it has filled its pot.
if_you_do: Fresh compost and a pot only a little bigger keep it growing without sitting wet.

normal: Slow, steady growth is normal now.
tips: Light: a sunny windowsill.
Water: when the compost is dry to the touch, then let it drain.
Feeding: once a month, April to September.
because: it is growing, and a monthly feed from April to September is enough.

normal: Growth slows ahead of the winter rest.
tips: Light: a sunny windowsill.
Water: less and less from October; no feed after September.
Warmth: away from radiators once the heating comes on.

normal: From mid-September a rest is normal, until flower buds appear: cool nights and dark evenings help the buds form.
tips: Light: bright but not full sun; no lamp near it after dark, or it may not flower.
Water: only once the compost has dried a few centimetres down.
Warmth: a cool room, about 12 to 15°C, helps it set buds.
Feeding: stop at the end of September.

normal: Flowering is normal from late November to late January.
tips: Light: bright, out of direct midday sun.
Water: when the top of the compost is dry; too much water can make buds drop.
Warmth: keep it steady; temperature swings and cold draughts make buds drop.
Air: mist it now and then, or stand it on a tray of damp gravel.

normal: A second rest after flowering is normal, until late March.
tips: Light: bright but not full sun.
Water: only once the compost has dried a few centimetres down.
Warmth: a cool room, about 12 to 15°C, never below 10°C.

normal: Its rest ends late in March, the time to repot.
tips: Light: bright but not full sun.
Water: only once the compost has dried a few centimetres down.
Repotting: at the end of March, if it has filled its pot.
because: the end of March is the time to repot a Christmas cactus.
if_you_do: Fresh compost at the start of its growing months.

normal: Growth is normal now: new segments form through summer.
tips: Light: bright, but not full sun.
Water: regularly, when the top of the compost starts to dry.
Warmth: 18 to 20°C suits it while it grows.
Feeding: from April to the end of September.
because: it is growing, and it is fed from April to the end of September.

normal: A flower spike now is normal: a moth orchid can flower at any time of year.
tips: Light: bright light helps it flower; an east or west windowsill is ideal.
Water: about once a week.
Warmth: above 16°C, away from radiators and draughts; cold makes buds drop.
Feeding: sparingly or not at all in winter.
because: bright winter light encourages it to flower.
if_you_do: A better chance of a flower spike in the coming months.

normal: New leaves and roots are normal now.
tips: Light: bright, but out of direct sun, which can scorch the leaves.
Water: about once a week.
Repotting: any time it needs it; fresh orchid compost every couple of years.
Feeding: regularly while it grows.

normal: Steady leaf and root growth is normal.
tips: Light: out of direct sun, which can scorch the leaves.
Water: about once a week.
Air: mist it daily in hot weather, or stand it on damp gravel.
because: hot weather dries the air it grows in.
if_you_do: Daily misting or a tray of damp gravel gives it the moist air it likes.

normal: A moth orchid can flower at any time of year, so no spike now is normal too.
tips: Light: bright, out of direct sun.
Water: about once a week.
Warmth: if it hasn't flowered for a while, a spot about 5°C cooler for a month can start a spike.

normal: Little new growth is normal in winter: daylight is weak.
tips: Light: out of dark corners to a brighter spot, and not behind closed curtains at night.
Water: less than in summer, when the top of the compost is dry.
Air: central heating dries the air; a tray of damp gravel or grouping plants helps.
Warmth: away from radiators, fires and cold draughts.
Feeding: little or none until March.
because: winter light is weak, and a dark corner gives weak, pale growth.
if_you_do: More light in winter means less weak, stretched growth.

normal: New growth is normal as the days lengthen.
tips: Light: bright, out of hot midday sun.
Water: more often as it grows; still let the top of the compost dry first.
Feeding: start again in March, following the label.
Repotting: spring is the time, if the roots fill the pot.

normal: Steady growth is normal now.
tips: Light: out of strong sun through the glass, which can scorch leaves.
Water: check more often in warm spells; never leave the pot standing in water.
Feeding: regularly until October, following the label.
because: it is growing, and houseplants are fed from March to October.

tips: Light: move it closer to a window as the light drops.
Water: less often as growth slows.
Warmth: when the heating comes on, keep it off radiators and out of draughts.
Feeding: from November, once a month at most.
because: the light is dropping, and a brighter spot keeps it growing steadily.
